newsitem.title: USA: Kodak January-February sales flat vs 1996.
newsitem.headline: Kodak January-February sales flat vs 1996.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co said its January and February sales were essentially flat compared with the first two months of last year.
Office imagining revenues were not included in the comparison, said Kodak.
The company did not provide specific figures and officials there were not immediately available to comment further.
Kodak said in a press statement that lower prices and the negative impact of foreign exchange offset modest unit volume growth in January and February.
The company also said its growth rates in emerging markets leveled off considerably compared with the first two months of 1996.

Harry Kavetas, Kodak's chief financial officer, said in the statement, "Although 1997 has started more slowly than we expected, there is nothing in these first months which would cause us to change our fundamental operating plans and objectives.
